section.title: Overview
section.simpara: The nginx JS DOM lets you read and write live nginx configuration from JavaScript running inside nginx workers. This guide covers the write-side of that API:

listitem.simpara: write_mode / read_mode — control where property assignments go and where reads come from (global shared struct vs per-request snapshot).
snapshot() / restore() — capture a point-in-time copy of a COM sub-tree and roll it back at any moment.

section.simpara: Together these two mechanisms let you implement safe hot-reload, per-tenant routing, A/B configuration experiments, and rollback-on-error patterns without reloading nginx.

entry.simpara: The C struct shared by all workers that was set up at config parse time. Mutations here affect every new request immediately.
A shallow copy of r->loc_conf[] (pointer array) plus deep copies of whatever individual C structs have been mutated for this request. Exists only for the duration of one request.
A JavaScript wrapper object (NginxLocation, NginxProxy, NginxPeer, NginxRRPeer, NginxUpstream, …) backed by a nginx C struct.

section.title: Default behaviour
section.simpara: Both write_mode and read_mode default to 'global'.
``` write_mode = global (default)
section.literallayout: Request N Global struct ────────── ───────────── req.location ──────────────────► clcf { root = '/new/root', ... } .root = '/new' │ │ visible to Request N+1 ▼ Request N+1 Global struct ────────── ───────────── req.location ──────────────────► clcf { root = '/new/root', ... } ```

entry.simpara: All property assignments write to the global shared C struct only. No per-request snapshot is created. Default.
Writes go to a per-request snapshot copy only. A snapshot is created automatically on the first write. The global struct is never touched. Other concurrent requests see the original global values.
Writes go to both the global struct and the per-request snapshot. Semantics of 'global' for other requests, semantics of 'local' for the current request.
Property reads always return the value from the global shared struct. Default.
Property reads prefer the per-request snapshot when one exists, falling back to the global struct automatically (because r->loc_conf[idx] == op->clcf until a snapshot is taken).

section.title: API
section.simpara: Both methods update the opaque state of the NginxLocation wrapper and propagate the new write_mode into the per-request context (rctx) so that sub-object setters (proxy, gzip, headers, rewrite) also honour it.

What snapshot() captures
section.simpara: obj.snapshot() reads the current visible values of all settable properties on obj (through read_mode) and stores them in a NginxSnapshot handle. For NginxLocation it also recursively captures the settable fields of sub-objects (proxy, gzip, headers, rewrite).

section.simpara: Null/undefined getter results are silently skipped (e.g. alias on a root-based location returns null and is not stored).

section.title: What restore() does
section.simpara: snap.restore() iterates all stored nodes and calls the standard property setter for each captured value using JS_SetPropertyStr.
The setter path handles:

listitem.simpara: ngx_js_ensure_core_snapshot() / ngx_js_ensure_module_snapshot() — creating per-request snapshot copies when needed.

section.simpara: restore() is best-effort: individual setter errors are silently cleared so that one failed field does not prevent others from being restored.
restore() is idempotent: you can call it multiple times safely.

section.title: restore() mode override
section.programlisting: snap.restore() // use current write_mode (default) snap.restore({ mode: 'global' }) // force all writes to global struct snap.restore({ mode: 'local' }) // force all writes to per-req snapshot snap.restore({ mode: 'both' }) // write to both
section.simpara: The override temporarily sets loc_op->write_mode and rctx->write_mode for the duration of the restore call, then restores the original values.

section.title: location.setWriteMode(mode)
section.simpara: Sets the write destination for property assignments on this location and its sub-objects.
Also propagates the new mode to rctx->write_mode so that sub-object setters (proxy, gzip, etc.) route writes consistently.

section.title: location.setReadMode(mode)
section.simpara: Sets the read source for property getters on this location.

entry.simpara: 'global' — always read from global shared struct. 'local' — prefer per-request snapshot; fall back to global.

section.title: location.snapshot()
section.simpara: Captures the current readable state of the location and all of its mutable sub-objects.
Returns a NginxSnapshot object. The snapshot is a point-in-time copy of every settable property value, read through the current read_mode.
Null/undefined property values are silently excluded.

section.title: upstream.snapshot()
section.simpara: Captures all peers in the upstream’s current peers[] array.
Each peer becomes a separate node in the snapshot. The snapshot is ordered (peer 0 first, backup peers last).

note.simpara: If peers are added or removed between snapshot() and restore(), the snapshot nodes point to the original peer objects (which remain valid as long as the upstream zone memory is not recycled). Restoring a snapshot after removePeer() may write to a peer that is no longer in the active list — this is harmless but produces no observable effect.

section.title: peer.snapshot() / rrPeer.snapshot()
section.simpara: Captures the five mutable fields of a single peer.

section.title: snap.restore([options])
section.simpara: Re-applies all captured values through the standard setter path.

entry.simpara: Optional string. When supplied, overrides the current write_mode for the duration of this restore call only. Original mode is restored after all fields are written.

listitem.simpara: Idempotent — calling restore() multiple times is safe.
Best-effort — individual setter errors are silently cleared.
Mode override applies to the location node and to rctx->write_mode so sub-object setters also use the requested mode.

section.title: NginxSnapshot (opaque object)
section.simpara: NginxSnapshot is an opaque QuickJS object with class name "NginxSnapshot". Its only JS-visible method is restore(). The captured values are not directly accessible from JavaScript.
The snapshot is garbage-collected when the last JS reference to it is dropped; no manual cleanup is required.

section.title: Internal snapshot vs JS snapshot
section.simpara: The internal C-level snapshot (ngx_js_ensure_core_snapshot, ngx_js_ensure_module_snapshot) is an automatic mechanism triggered by write_mode='local' setters. It operates at the C struct level and is invisible to JavaScript.
The JS-level snapshot() / restore() operates at the property level: it calls the existing getters and setters. The two mechanisms are complementary:

listitem.simpara: write_mode='local' + internal snapshots → isolation of mutations.

section.title: Why restore() is best-effort
section.simpara: Some setters may legitimately fail (e.g. alias on a root-based location throws a type error). Because snapshot() silently skips null/undefined values (and alias returns null for root-based locations), such fields are never captured. The restore() "best-effort" guarantee handles any remaining edge cases — e.g. a location type changed between snapshot and restore — without crashing the request.

section.title: Snapshot scope for upstream.snapshot()
section.simpara: upstream.snapshot() captures the current peer array. If peers are added via addPeer() after the snapshot, those new peers are not in the snapshot and will not be removed by restore(). Similarly, if peers are removed via removePeer(), restoring field values to a removed peer has no effect on the live upstream.
For a complete "undo addPeer/removePeer", use the addPeer()/removePeer() methods directly rather than relying on snapshot().
